security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when senvcfg.MT_ASYNC=1 (or menvcfg.MT_ASYNC=1 for M-mode) and a regular store triggers a tag mismatch, the fault is deferred. The pending mismatch is resolved on the next trap (any exception or interrupt) by setting stval2 to the faulting virtual address. If the kernel's context-switch path (__switch_to) does not save and restore stval2, and a timer interrupt during context switch resolves a pending mismatch from the outgoing process, then (a) the fault address is lost, corrupting si_addr in SIGSEGV delivery, or (b) the fault address from the outgoing process is spuriously attributed to the incoming process, leaking cross-process address layout. Similarly, in KVM, htval2 must be saved/restored on vCPU switch to prevent cross-VM address leakage.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: thread_struct lacks stval2 field; __switch_to lacks CSR read/write of stval2; do_trap_insn_* or handle_exception does not read stval2 for EXC_SW_CHECK (tval=4); kvm_riscv_vcpu_switch lacks htval2 save/restore
security_spec.summary: New stval2/htval2/mtval3 CSRs capture tag-mismatch fault virtual address resolve-on-next-trap in async mode; kernel must save/restore these CSRs on context switch and KVM vCPU switch to prevent address leaks and corrupted signal delivery
